chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Asim, from his father, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and in his hand was an ivory comb with which he combed himself. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! There are some among us in Iraq who claim that it is not permissible to comb with ivory.' He said, 'And why? For there used to be from my father (peace be upon him) one or two combs of ivory.' Then he said, 'Comb with ivory, for ivory removes the illness (fever).'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use an ivory comb according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the claim that using ivory combs is forbidden by citing his own practice and that of his father, establishing a precedent of permissibility (halal) within the Shia tradition. He further highlights the therapeutic virtue of ivory, noting its ability to dispel illness or fever, which aligns with the broader Islamic emphasis on utilizing natural materials for health benefits. This narration serves both as a legal ruling on material usage and as a practical medical recommendation found in the traditions of the Imams.
